item.text: Soak passed: 64 committed entries under 8 churn rounds, no losses. Let me record it.

This pass added a direct safety probe rather than relying only on the project's own tests. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-08_13-11-14-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

**New executed evidence — committed-entry churn soak**

`TestAudit_CommittedEntriesSurviveChurn` (`audit/soak.log`) spins up a 5-node in-memory cluster and, repeatedly, drives commands while isolating the current leader (forcing re-elections) and then healing it. It records every command for which `Apply` returned nil (i.e. committed) and afterwards asserts each one is present on every replica — a disappearing committed entry would violate Raft's core safety property. Result: **2/2 runs passed**, 64 committed entries over 8 churn rounds per run, every replica retaining every committed entry.

That is meaningful negative evidence for leader-election/log-matching safety, but I've labeled it explicitly as a small, bounded sample that does not cover disk persistence, restarts, or snapshot/compaction under churn.

**State of the audit**

- Finding 1 stands: `testing.go:692-715` `EnsureSamePeers` caches `c.rafts[0]`'s configuration and never refreshes it, yielding spurious `testing.go:705 peer mismatch` failures across its 10 callers (measured 3/120 in a focused campaign; root cause isolated and the one-line fix verified 20/20).
- Secondary suspicion recorded but not observed: `EnsureLeader` (`testing.go:582-604`) is the only assertion helper with no retry/timeout.
- No defect found in the core consensus/agreement logic; artifact remains byte-identical to upstream v1.7.3 (no planted mutation). `source/` untouched; additions confined to `audit/`, `audit_diag_test.go`, and `report.md`.
